claims.text: Rapid quenching produces HfNbTaTiZr with a highly disordered atomic configuration and minimal chemical short-range order.
Controlled slow cooling or annealing increases chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr relative to rapid quenching.
Increased chemical short-range order promotes the formation of locally ordered domains.
Locally ordered domains stabilize specific interatomic distances.
Stabilization of interatomic distances by local ordering reduces the activation of anharmonic vibrational modes.
Reduced anharmonic lattice vibrations lower the thermal expansion coefficient.
Reduced anharmonic lattice vibrations diminish the degradation of elastic modulus with increasing temperature.
Local chemical order produces heterogeneous internal stresses under applied stress.
Heterogeneous internal stresses associated with local order generate inflections or nonlinear regions in elevated-temperature stress–strain curves.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will have a lower thermal expansion coefficient than as-quenched samples.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will exhibit less elastic-modulus softening with increasing temperature than as-quenched samples.
Slow-cooled or annealed samples will exhibit stress–strain anomalies that are absent or less pronounced in the as-quenched baseline.
The predicted stress–strain anomalies will correlate with abrupt changes in lattice parameters.
Diffraction peak shifts and intensities can be used to assess CSRO-related local lattice distortions.
Atom-probe-tomography atom-to-atom ordering statistics can directly quantify the degree of CSRO.
The proposed CSRO-mediated behavior is expected to hold from 25°C to 900°C.
Above 900°C, phase transformations or diffusion-driven processes may dominate the response.
